newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to sell motor boats, marine engines.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to sell motor boats, marine engines.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp said on Wednesday that it would start selling motorboats and marine engines in Japan next spring.
Toyota plans to sell a 28-foot cabin-cruiser, which was designed and developed by Toyota and will be produced in New Zealand, Toyota said in a statement.
The Japanese car maker will handle sales of the model, which are not expected to be high in the initial stage, it said.
It also plans to sell two marine engines -- one diesel and the other gasoline.
Toyota said it eventually plans to develop a range of boats of varying sizes and a full line-up of marine engines, as well as establish a consultancy business to provide information on marine sports.
This would be the first time for Toyota, Japan's biggest car maker, to get involved in the marine market.
The boats will be made by two New Zealand boat makers -- Circa Engineering & Marine Ltd and Mcdell Marine Ltd.

"We want to sell the best boats -- so in the first year, we plan to sell a limited number of 15 boats. We have set an annual sales target for 50 billion yen worth of boat sales for the year 2000," Kosuke Yamamoto, a Toyota executive vice president, told Reuters.
Yamamoto also said that Toyota would soon announce plans to supply boat engines to an American boat maker.
The boat venture would add to a number of Toyota businesses outside of automobile manufacturing. Others include telecommunications, autoparts retailing and housing.

Toyota plans to continue promoting its non-automobile business, Toyota president Hiroshi Okuda said. Okuda said the company is aiming for sales in the non-automobile business of around one trillion yen by the year 2000, which would be 10 percent of its overall targeted parent sales.
